findings.title: Toter Include <cache_engine/measurement/system_axis.hpp> zieht die measurement-Schicht (observable_tier + pmc_source) cross-layer in jeden Konsumenten
findings.scenario: Bewiesen: axis_binding_registry.hpp referenziert KEIN einziges Symbol aus system_axis.hpp (grep: nur die Include-Zeile 19 selbst matcht 'system_axis'). Entfernt man Zeile 19, kompiliert der Header fehlerfrei auf g++-16 UND clang-22 (fsyntax-only sauber; nosys.hpp ist byte-identisch zum Original minus der Include-Zeile). Der Kommentar gibt selbst zu, dass der Include 'nur fuer die measurement-Layer-Naht/Doku' da ist. Folge: jede Translation Unit, die axis_binding_registry.hpp (builder/axis_binding-Schicht) inkludiert, zieht transitiv system_axis.hpp + anatomy/observable_tier.hpp + builder/pmc_source.hpp + measurement/measurement_category.hpp mit (gemessen: 240 vs. 234 Header via g++ -H). Das koppelt die reine constexpr-Klassifikationsschicht unnoetig an die measurement/observable/pmc-Schicht -- exakt das im Phase-6-Review gefundene tote-Include-Muster.

findings.title: Cap-WERTE (4096/1GiB/64/64/256) sind nicht compile-time an abi_adapter gekoppelt; consteval-Guard prueft nur cap != 0
findings.scenario: registry_is_consistent() prueft in Zeile 107 nur is_dyn <=> (rc_cap != 0), NIE den konkreten Cap-Wert. Dieselben fuenf Caps liegen dreifach dupliziert: hier (kAxisBindingRegistry, Zeilen 69-80), in abi_adapter.hpp:226-231 (tier_query_resource_caps, Runtime-Member) und im Laufzeit-Test:71-75. Es gibt keine static_assert-Kopplung der Werte an abi_adapter (der sizeof-Assert Zeile 129 koppelt nur die ANZAHL an den POD, nicht die Werte). Aendert jemand abi_adapter's Cap (z.B. thread_count 64->128), bricht KEIN static_assert; nur der Laufzeit-Test, der 64 ebenfalls hartcodiert, muesste manuell nachgezogen werden -> stiller Drift moeglich.

findings.title: axis_binding(slot_index) ist noexcept ohne Bounds-Check (std::array::operator[]) -> Runtime-UB bei Out-of-Range-Index
findings.scenario: axis_binding(std::size_t) gibt kAxisBindingRegistry[slot_index] via unchecked array::operator[] zurueck (noexcept, kein assert, kein .at()). Ein Aufruf mit slot_index >= 19 (z.B. Slot-Index aus einer Laufzeit-/untrusted-Quelle) ist stiller UB statt eines definierten Fehlers. Compile-time-Aufrufe mit OOB-Index sind hingegen sicher (ill-formed). Aktuell existiert kein Aufrufer mit dynamischem Index (Test nutzt nur 0 und 8), daher latent -- aber die Signatur akzeptiert beliebige size_t.

findings.title: Wrong-direction, cyclic AND unused cross-layer include of measurement/system_axis.hpp (Baseline-Layering-Verstoss)
findings.scenario: The registry (builder layer) #includes <cache_engine/measurement/system_axis.hpp>, but system_axis.hpp:10 itself includes ../../../builder/pmc_source.hpp (= libs/cache_engine/builder/pmc_source.hpp) and anatomy/observable_tier.hpp — i.e. measurement is a CONSUMER of builder and sits ABOVE it. So builder->measurement references a higher tier, violating the doctrine 'nur niederwertigere referenzieren', and creates a builder<->measurement include cycle. Worse, the include is dead: no symbol from system_axis.hpp is used anywhere in the registry (only ex::kCompositionAxisNames from experiment_tree and ComdareResourceControlV1 from anatomy are used); the comment itself concedes it is '(nur fuer die measurement-Layer-Naht/Doku)'. Deleting line 19 changes nothing at compile time, proving it is gratuitous wrong-direction coupling that only adds a cycle. (By contrast the anatomy include is a valid downward direction — genus_binding_traits.hpp already includes anatomy/*.)

findings.title: RC cap values are copied literals from abi_adapter with no compile-time cross-check -> silent drift
findings.scenario: The caps 4096 (L69), 1<<30 (L75), 64 (L76), 64 (L77), 256 (L80) are hand-copied from abi_adapter.hpp:226-231 (tier_query_resource_caps). The consteval guards only check the field COUNT (sizeof(POD)/8-1 == 5) and the RcField bijection — none tie rc_cap to the actual abi_adapter cap VALUES (tier_query_resource_caps is a non-constexpr member, so it cannot back a static_assert here). If someone raises e.g. thread_count from 64 to 128 in abi_adapter.hpp:226, the registry's rc_cap=64 (L77) and the test's hard-coded expectation (test_axis_binding_registry.cpp:71) both stay green while silently reporting the stale cap. The registry is therefore a second, unsynchronised copy of the caps, not a derived Single-Source.

findings.title: Doppelt-Wahrheit: the 14/5 compile-dynamic axis classification already lives in profile_to_tree.hpp, which is the ACTUAL tree producer; the registry has zero consumers
findings.scenario: profile_to_tree.hpp:76-87 already classifies the exact same 5 axes (concurrency/prefetch/allocator/cache_traversal/value_handle) as dynamic via the is_static=false flag on the emitted AxisLevel — and that flag is what literally becomes StaticAxisNode vs DynamicVariableNode in the B+ tree (the authoritative producer). profile_to_tree.hpp:68-70 explicitly declares build_axis_levels 'DIE EINZIGE Quelle dieser Dimensionen' after a prior Doppelquelle (profile_runner::profile_dynamic_dims) was consolidated on 2026-06-18. runtime_variable_loop.hpp:53-60 independently hard-codes the same var->POD-field mapping again. The new registry re-introduces the identical classification as a THIRD parallel encoding, yet grep shows it has zero consumers (nothing outside the header+test references kAxisBindingRegistry / for_each_axis_binding). Nothing links the registry to profile_to_tree, so the two can diverge: a future 6th dynamic axis would trip the registry's sizeof(POD) static_assert but profile_to_tree would keep emitting the old set (or vice-versa) with no compile-time contradiction. The header's 'Single-Source' claim is therefore false — it is a drift-prone duplicate, not a consolidation.

findings.title: Fork-independence claim cites Doc 20 §H, which does not exist in-repo; cache_traversal(T1) is frozen as a design constant on an unverifiable basis
findings.scenario: The header grounds its KK-1 'Design-Konstante' and 'Fork-UNABHAENGIG ... 7 User-Forks aus Doc 20 §H' on docs/architektur/20_...md §B/§G/§H. But the repo's Doc 20 is docs/architecture/20_plugin_controller_pruefling_loading.md (cache-engine as Plugin-Controller), organised in numeric sections §1/§2..., with no §B/§G/§H and no compile/dynamic Messkurven-Typsystem; the cited path spelling ('architektur') is not even the repo's ('architecture'). So the (b) fork-independence guarantee cannot be verified in-repo. Concretely: cache_traversal (slot L01 = T1) is hard-classified Dynamic/BatchSize (L69) and locked by consteval static_asserts (L121-131). If §H point 7 genuinely leaves T1's attribution open (as the review hypothesis states), the registry silently pre-commits that open user decision as an immutable constant — but neither the openness nor the §H citation can be substantiated from this repository (the doc may live out-of-repo in super docs/, so this is a grounding gap, not a proven mis-classification).

result.reason: CONFIRMED by empirical reproduction against the live repo. The five caps in axis_binding_registry.hpp (L69=4096, L75=1<<30, L76=64, L77=64, L80=256) are hand-typed literals; the caps in abi_adapter.hpp:226-231 are independent hand-typed literals in a non-constexpr virtual member (tier_query_resource_caps, pure-virtual at resource_controllable_tier.hpp:63 — genuinely cannot back a static_assert). Grep confirms NO shared single-source constant links them — only a comment. The consteval guards (registry_is_consistent, count_dynamic==5, count_compile==14, sizeof(POD)/8-1==count_dynamic) check only structure: names, Dynamic<=>rc_cap!=0, RcField bijection, field count — none compares rc_cap to the abi_adapter VALUES. Grep shows the registry's rc_cap has zero external consumers/cross-checks. Drift is concretely reproducible: raising thread_count 64->128 at abi_adapter.hpp:226 leaves registry L77 rc_cap=64 and test_axis_binding_registry.cpp:71 (which reads the REGISTRY, not the live cap) both green, and all consteval guards green (they only require rc_cap!=0). Note test_e2_contract_abi_vertrag.cpp:81 reads the LIVE cap and would fail — but that only forces updating test_e2, giving no signal to fix the stale registry copy. The registry is thus a second (and its test a third) unsynchronised copy of the caps, not a derived Single-Source — directly contradicting the file's own 'GEERDET (nie geraten)'/Single-Source claim and 'Achtung Drift-Falle' note. Severity major (layering-scope) is justified: the file adds count/sizeof drift-guards but conspicuously omits the value guard. The current value 64 is correct, so this is a maintainability/architecture defect (silent-drift hazard), not a present runtime bug.

FALSE POSITIVE (adversarial verdict). The technical facts are all accurate: axis_binding(std::size_t) at libs/cache_engine/builder/axis_binding/axis_binding_registry.hpp:134-136 is noexcept and returns kAxisBindingRegistry[slot_index] via unchecked std::array::operator[] with no bounds check / no .at() / no assert. I empirically confirmed both behavioral claims in an isolated scratch dir (official build/ untouched): a compile-time OOB call is ill-formed (static_assert(axis_binding(5)...) -> "error: non-constant condition for static assertion"), and a runtime OOB call is silent UB in a plain -O2 build (probe read out-of-bounds, exited 0, no diagnostic; under ASAN/_GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS it aborts, but the official CMake sets no hardening flags).

However the FAILURE SCENARIO is not concretely reproducible or compelling in this codebase, so real=false: (1) Exhaustive grep shows the ONLY caller of axis_binding( anywhere is tests/unit/test_axis_binding_registry.cpp using compile-time literal constants 0 and 8, both in-bounds. NO caller passes a dynamic/runtime/untrusted index — the finding itself concedes "Aktuell existiert kein Aufrufer mit dynamischem Index ... daher latent". The "untrusted runtime source" is invented ("z.B. ..."), not present. (2) The unchecked-lookup idiom is the ESTABLISHED, explicitly-mirrored codebase pattern: the sibling measurement_axis_registry.hpp — which this file's header declares it follows ("nach dem Muster measurement_axis_registry.hpp") — uses the identical noexcept unchecked `return kMeasurementAxisRegistry[static_cast<std::size_t>(c)];` (lines 65-66). (3) This is idiomatic standard C++ (std::array::operator[] is unchecked by design); labeling it a defect describes STL behavior, not a bug. (4) The documented design intent (header: "KEIN Runtime-Switch ... reine constexpr-Klassifikation") is compile-time metaprogramming use, where OOB is ill-formed and caught. Grounding sources all verified correct (kCompositionAxisNames, ComdareResourceControlV1 fields, caps 4096/1GiB/64/64/256). A UB program can only be produced by an artificial caller I write myself, mirroring any STL operator[] — which does not demonstrate a defect in this repo. Under the rule "real=true NUR wenn das Fehl-Szenario konkret reproduzierbar/zwingend ist; bei Unsicherheit real=false", this is a latent [minor] defensive-programming/API-hardening suggestion, not a reproducible failure.

CONFIRMED at the real repo stand (uncommitted libs/cache_engine/builder/axis_binding/axis_binding_registry.hpp, verified via git status). (1) grep shows 'system_axis' appears on exactly ONE line: the include on line 19 itself — no symbol usage. (2) Decisive compile probe: a copy with line 19 removed (both other includes intact: axis_path_serialization + resource_controllable_tier) compiles cleanly with -fsyntax-only on BOTH g++-16 (exit 0) AND clang++-22 (exit 0), C++23, using the real CMake include roots (libs/cache_engine, .../include, .../src, .../builder). Because measurement_category.hpp/observable_tier.hpp/pmc_source.hpp are reachable ONLY through system_axis.hpp (they vanish completely from the stripped -H output), a clean compile proves no symbol from that subtree is used — including all consteval/static_assert gates, which fire under -fsyntax-only and still pass. (3) g++ -H measures the coupling: the dead include drags in 6 repo headers (total distinct 202 -> 196, delta exactly 6 as the claim's 240->234 states): system_axis.hpp, measurement_category.hpp, anatomy/observable_tier.hpp, builder/pmc_source.hpp, plus transitively anatomy/idriveable_tier.hpp and anatomy/measurable_workload.hpp — every header the claim named is present, and it actually undercounts by two (coupling is worse, not weaker). (4) Line 19's own comment admits the include is 'nur fuer die measurement-Layer-Naht/Doku', i.e. not functionally needed, and it couples the pure constexpr builder/axis_binding classification layer to the measurement/observable/pmc layer — violating the project's stated layering doctrine (Organ- vs System-Achsen nie vermischen; Phase-6 dead-include pattern). Failure scenario is concrete, reproducible on both toolchains, and zwingend. real=true.

CONFIRMED empirically at real repo stand. The consteval guard registry_is_consistent() at axis_binding_registry.hpp:107 checks only `is_dyn != (rc_cap != 0)` — non-zero-ness, never the concrete cap value. Compile-probe (scratch only, no repo/build/git writes): copying the header with concurrency cap 64->128 compiles CLEAN with -fsyntax-only (no static_assert fires); the same copy with cap 64->0 DOES trip the static_assert at line 121. This proves the guard does not couple the value. The sizeof-assert at lines 129-131 couples only the COUNT (sizeof(ComdareResourceControlV1)/8 - 1 == count_dynamic()==5), not any value. The registry does NOT #include abi_adapter.hpp (only resource_controllable_tier.hpp for the POD) and references abi_adapter solely in comments; abi_adapter::tier_query_resource_caps (abi_adapter.hpp:226-231) writes the caps at RUNTIME in a non-constexpr noexcept member, so there is literally no compile-time constant to static_assert against. The five caps are duplicated in four places (registry 69-80; abi_adapter 226-231; test_axis_binding_registry.cpp 71-75; test_e2_contract_abi_vertrag.cpp 81-85) — the finding's 'triple' is understated. Drift is concrete and reproducible: changing abi_adapter thread_count 64->128 breaks NO static_assert; the registry's own test still passes (it verifies registry==64, not registry vs abi_adapter); only test_e2_contract_abi_vertrag.cpp:81 fails at runtime, and updating that hardcoded 64->128 leaves the registry silently at 64 with nothing detecting the registry<->abi_adapter divergence — exactly the silent value-drift claimed. Finding's minor imprecisions (4 copies not 3; the catching test is the E2 contract test, not the registry's own test) make the gap worse, not better, and do not undermine the core metaprog-strictness claim.

CONFIRMED major layering-scope violation. Every factual claim reproduced at the live repo stand (ce HEAD c022ce0; registry + test are uncommitted, git status: ?? libs/cache_engine/builder/axis_binding/, ?? tests/unit/test_axis_binding_registry.cpp, M tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt).

(1) DIRECTION/CYCLE. axis_binding_registry.hpp:19 (namespace comdare::cache_engine::builder::axis_binding) does `#include <cache_engine/measurement/system_axis.hpp>`. That header (found at libs/cache_engine/include/cache_engine/measurement/system_axis.hpp, namespace ...::measurement) at line 10 includes `../../../builder/pmc_source.hpp` and at line 9 `../../../anatomy/observable_tier.hpp`, and actually USES builder::PmcCounters (line 284, `using counters_t = ::comdare::cache_engine::builder::PmcCounters`). So measurement is a CONSUMER of builder and sits ABOVE it; builder→measurement therefore references a higher tier, violating the baseline doctrine "eine Baseline darf ausschliesslich Interfaces NIEDERWERTIGERER Baselines referenzieren" (feedback_baseline_system_in_stein_gemeisselt_layering, Regel 1). It is simultaneously a builder⇄measurement layer-dependency cycle (builder axis_binding → measurement/system_axis → builder/pmc_source).

(2) DEAD INCLUDE. grep of the registry finds no measurement-namespace symbol (SystemAxis/MeasurementCategory/MeasurementRegime/...): line 19 is the include itself and line 4 is only a prose reference to measurement_axis_registry.hpp as a pattern. The only external symbols used are ex::kCompositionAxisNames (from builder/experiment_tree/axis_path_serialization.hpp:30-34, verified) and anatomy::ComdareResourceControlV1 (from anatomy/resource_controllable_tier.hpp:34-40, verified). The line-19 comment itself concedes "(nur fuer die measurement-Layer-Naht/Doku)".

(3) EMPIRICAL COMPILE PROOF (scratch, g++ 16.0.1 -std=c++23 -fsyntax-only, official build/ untouched, no git write). A copy of the header with line 19 deleted compiles cleanly (NO19_OK) with all consteval static_asserts firing, identical to the original (ORIG_OK). `g++ -M` dependency-set diff: the ORIGINAL TU pulls system_axis.hpp, measurement_category.hpp, anatomy/observable_tier.hpp, anatomy/idriveable_tier.hpp, anatomy/measurable_workload.hpp AND builder/pmc_source.hpp; the STRIPPED TU pulls NONE of these. This proves the wrong-direction/cyclic measurement→builder edge is introduced SOLELY by line 19 and is gratuitous (deleting it changes nothing at compile time).

(4) CONTRAST claim also holds: the sibling anatomy include is a valid downward reference — genus_binding_traits.hpp (builder/experiment_tree) already includes anatomy/anatomy_base.hpp, composition_factory.hpp, etc. (lines 13-19), so builder→anatomy is the established downward pattern.

Minor wording nuance: at strict file granularity it is not an A→B→A self-cycle (axis_binding_registry.hpp is not re-included); it is a LAYER cycle builder⇄measurement, which is precisely the granularity the baseline-layering doctrine governs — so the finding's "builder<->measurement include cycle" characterization is accurate. Fault scenario is concretely reproducible and compelling.

CONFIRMED at real repo state (uncommitted axis_binding_registry.hpp). Core claims all empirically verified: (1) Zero production consumers — grep for kAxisBindingRegistry/for_each_axis_binding/AxisBindingInfo/axis_binding:: hits only tests/unit/test_axis_binding_registry.cpp; no production file includes or references the header. (2) The identical 5-axis dynamic classification (concurrency/prefetch/allocator/cache_traversal/value_handle) already lives in profile_to_tree.hpp:75-87 via is_static=false, and experiment_tree.hpp:342-354 (static_filter/dynamic_filter) shows is_static literally drives StaticAxisNode vs DynamicDim — so profile_to_tree is the authoritative tree producer, as the finding states. (3) profile_to_tree.hpp:68-70 explicitly declares itself 'DIE EINZIGE Quelle dieser Dimensionen' after consolidating a prior Doppelquelle (2026-06-18); runtime_variable_loop.hpp:52-63 independently hard-codes the same 5-way var->POD mapping; abi_adapter.hpp:226-231 encodes the same 5 caps — so the registry is a 3rd/4th parallel encoding. (4) No compile-time coupling registry<->profile_to_tree (no include, no cross static_assert); the registry's guards only bind it to kCompositionAxisNames names + ComdareResourceControlV1 sizeof. The drift scenario is mechanically valid: a future non-POD dynamic axis (exactly like the existing hw_prefetcher/repetition is_static=false architectural exceptions in profile_to_tree) would be emitted by the producer while the registry's sizeof(POD) assert stays green — silent divergence with no compile-time contradiction.

Nuances that do NOT invalidate the finding: the header's literal 'Single-Source' tag (line 12) refers to the axis NAMES (kCompositionAxisNames), which is accurate, so the finding slightly overstates in calling that claim 'false'; and the registry is partially self-guarded (POD sizeof + name asserts catch POD-field additions), so it is not wholly ungrounded. But it is genuinely uncoupled from the actual tree producer, currently consumer-less, and a drift-prone duplicate — which in a codebase with an explicit documented anti-Doppelquelle/Single-Source doctrine (prior 2026-06-18 consolidation) is a legitimate major layering-scope/double-truth defect reproducible at the current code state.

REFUTED by empirical reproduction against the real working tree. The finding's premise — that the header's Doc 20 §G/§H grounding is unverifiable and cache_traversal(T1)'s Dynamic classification is "frozen on an unverifiable basis" — is false.

The header (axis_binding_registry.hpp:7-10) cites "Doc 20 §G/§H", not a filesystem path. The cache-engine submodule's own docs/architecture/20_plugin_controller_pruefling_loading.md is indeed a different doc (§1-§6, Plugin-Controller topic), but the referenced project-wide ledger Doc 20 exists one level up in the umbrella repo: /home/comdare/Projekte/Research/probst-diplomarbeit-cache-engine/docs/architektur/20_HEURISTIK_MESSKURVEN_TYPSYSTEM_UND_FILTERKETTE.md. It contains lettered sections that match every citation: "## B. Das Messkurven-Typsystem", "## G. Kardinalitäts-Synthese" (KK-1 = "compile-time-fix — Kardinalität = Design-Konstante"), and "## H. Offene Punkte" listing exactly SEVEN numbered User-Forks ("7 User-Forks" is exact).

The fork-independence claim is substantiated word-for-word: §H lines 111-112 state "Diese sieben Forks bestimmen die Map-Schlüssel-Kardinalitäten ... die tree<axis compile/dynamic>-Wurzel (§G Zeile 1) ist davon UNABHÄNGIG und wird zuerst gebaut." So the header's "Fork-UNABHAENGIG" is directly quoting the design doc, not inventing a guarantee.

The review's hypothesis that §H point 7 "leaves T1's attribution open" and the registry silently pre-commits it is wrong: §H point 7's T1 item is a MEASUREMENT-separability constraint (T1 overlaps T5+T7; isolated attribution needs fixed T5/T7 in a micro-bench — BEFUND-KARDINALITAETEN.md:160-165,210,226), which is orthogonal to the compile/dynamic binding of the composition axis. §H explicitly declares that compile/dynamic root split settled and independent of all 7 forks.

Finally, cache_traversal=Dynamic/BatchSize (L69, Cap 4096) is grounded in the ABI-frozen RC-POD, not guessed: resource_controllable_tier.hpp:38 declares "std::uint64_t batch_size = 0; // Achse traversal (axis_03a)", and the deep-research befund lists "T1 batch_size" among the 5 RC-POD dynamic axes with Cap 4096. All consteval guards (RC bijection, count 5/14, sizeof-POD coupling) are consistent with this grounding.

The path-spelling objection is moot (the header cites no path; "architektur" is correct for the umbrella ledger). The fail-scenario is not reproducible: the citation is accurate, locatable within the diplomarbeit working tree, and fully substantiates the header's claims.
